item.title: Resettled, not rehabilitated: Inside India’s ‘climate colony’
item.description: Displaced by coastal erosion, people began moving to Bagapatia in the 2010s, but continue to decry the village’s inadequate and dangerous conditions.

item.title: Proposed ‘community mines' in Sumatra raise red flags
item.description: The devolved government in West Sumatra province, which is home to 5.8 million people on Indonesia’s Sumatra Island, intends to present new zoning plans to the central government that could regulate currently illegal mines operated by small groups of people.

item.title: Philippines greenlights first large waste-to-energy project
item.description: The move comes at the heels of recent trash slides in the provinces of Rizal and Cebu, which have intensified scrutiny of the country’s landfill‑dependent waste system.

item.title: Taiwan to launch voluntary circular label scheme for plastics, textiles in March
item.description: Flexible certification aims to boost recycling and reuse models, with approved products prioritised in government procurement under 2050 circular economy plan.

item.title: Faster, coordinated action needed to deliver Asia’s energy transition: Energy Asia
item.description: Rising energy demand and rapid economic growth are constantly reshaping Asia’s transition challenge.

item.title: China’s new renewables pricing mechanism may not give generators the stability they need
item.description: As subsidies for renewables are phased out, market distortions mean renewables still can’t stand on their own feet.

item.title: AI is becoming the new engine of climate risk assessment – should we be worried?
item.description: Are organisations ready for the governance, accountability and strategic implications that come with handing climate analysis to algorithms?

item.title: Juan Miguel Cuna appointed as Philippines’ acting environment secretary
item.description: Cuna replaces Raphael Lotilla, as the outgoing environment chief is designated to be the country's ambassador to the Vatican.

item.title: Australia spends US$18 billion more harming nature than protecting it, study finds
item.description: A new study finds Australia spends far more on subsidies that harm biodiversity than on conservation, underscoring the need to reform fiscal policy to meet its 2030 global nature targets.

item.title: Rethinking coal phase-out in Asia and beyond
item.description: To accelerate the retirement of coal, we need a scalable incentive framework that offers equitable participation and fair distribution of costs and benefits.
